_source: Authored against docs/design/data/tpt-vocabulary.json (taxonomyTags, category Type-of-Resource, polled 2026-09-03) and docs/design/data/tes-vocabulary.json (resourceTypes, the nine values the uploader's type select admits). No network contact.
_status: DRAFT awaiting founder confirmation, drafted 2026-09-03. Twenty-one authored rows cover all 71 facets: ten roots, eleven child overrides, and 50 children that inherit their root.

kindMeaning.narrower: The facet is narrower than the one named Tes value, so the facet's own canonical term holds a Broader edge into the Tes path. Every row here is narrower, because Tes carries nine values against TPT's seventy-one: the relation is many-to-one, which is legal only through Broader (docs/design/taxonomy-projection.md:36-37).
kindMeaning.null: Hidden. It seeds neither term nor edge, on ruling C.

inheritance: A child not named below takes its root's value. Fifty of the sixty-one children inherit; the eleven that do not are named because inheriting would file them under a value Tes distinguishes from the right one.

pairs.rationale: Bulletin boards, posters and word walls are display material, which is what `Visual aid/Display` names.
A graphic asset the seller drops into their own material; Tes files it as display rather than as an activity.
Proposals, nurse documents and council paperwork answer to no Tes type, and `Other` is the value Tes offers for exactly that.
`Worksheet/Activity` carries the word; the members that are genuinely games or audio override below.
Hidden, so it seeds no edge and arrives as an unrecognised slug retained verbatim, on the same rule as a hidden subject facet.
Handouts, scaffolded notes and guided readers are the material of a taught lesson.
The printable is the worksheet, and Tes names them with one value.
`Assessment and revision` is the same category under a different name.
Homework, task cards and workbooks are activity material rather than a taught lesson.
The root is genuinely mixed -- planners, rubrics, syllabi and unit plans -- so it takes `Other` and its members override where Tes has a real value for them.
A game is the one thing `Game/puzzle/quiz` names, and inheriting `Worksheet/Activity` would file it under the wrong one of two values Tes distinguishes.
An escape room is a puzzle, and Tes separates puzzles from worksheets.
Audio material, which Tes carries as `Audio, music & video` and nowhere else.
`Unit of work` is Tes's name for the same artefact.
A unit of work with a theme is still a unit of work.
A year of planned work is a unit of work at its largest, and Tes offers no coarser value.
A curriculum is planned work rather than a teacher's tool.
A syllabus states the planned work for a course.
`Lesson (complete)` is the value, and inheriting `Other` from the root would discard an exact match Tes offers.
A lecture is the delivered form of a complete lesson.
A rubric is assessment material, which Tes carries under `Assessment and revision`.
